chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and Abd al-Malik al-Qummi entered upon him and said, 'May Allah improve your state; do I prostrate while my hand is inside my garment?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'If you wish.' Then he (peace be upon him) said, 'By Allah, I do not fear for you because of this and things similar to it.'

key_terms.وَيَدِي فِي ثَوْبِي: and my hand is in my garment

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to keep one hand inside the garment while prostrating in prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle of ease (yusr) in ritual prayer, where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of keeping the hand concealed within the garment during prostration. The Imam’s subsequent remark, 'I do not fear for you,' underscores the reliability of this practice among the early Shia community, distinguishing it from acts that might invalidate the prayer or require strict uniformity. It serves as a foundational text for the flexibility in sunnah actions of prayer, provided the core pillars are maintained.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdul Rahman Bin Al Hajjaj who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, and Abdul Malik Al-Qummy came over to him<sup>asws</sup> and he said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! Can I prostrate while my hand is inside my clothes?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If you so desire to’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: I, ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>!; am not afraid for you because of this and things similar to it’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who has said the following:

“I once was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when ‘Abd al-Malik al-Qummiy came and asked saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, I perform Sajdah (prostration) and my hands are inside my clothes. He (the Imam) said, ‘If you want, you can do so.’ He (the narrator) has said that he (the Imam) then said, ‘I, by Allah, am not afraid for you because of this and things similar to it.’”
